The test image shows corn ear kernels with white/cottony fluffy mycelial growth between and around pale yellowish kernels. This is an ear rot. Key candidates: Diplodia_Ear_Rot, Trichoderma_Ear_Rot, Fusarium_Disease, Aspergillus_Ear_Rot.

Let me view reference images one at a time starting with the most likely candidates.
Not matching well. Let me check Trichoderma_Ear_Rot.
Trichoderma shows green mold - doesn't match the white mycelium in the test image. Let me check Fusarium_Disease.
Partial match - white mycelium on kernels, but test image has more complete/fluffy white coverage. Let me check Gibberella_Disease.
Gibberella shows pink/red discoloration - doesn't match. Let me check Aspergillus_Ear_Rot.
Aspergillus shows olive/green powdery mold - doesn't match. Let me check a second Diplodia_Ear_Rot reference for the white cottony mycelium.
This Diplodia reference shows white mycelium between kernels - getting closer. Let me check the third Diplodia reference.
I've visited 5 classes with 7 views. I need 1 more view from a new class to complete the budget.

Common Smut shows black galls - clearly doesn't match.

**Summary of observations:**
- Test image: corn ear kernels with dense white/cottony fluffy mycelium covering and between pale yellowish kernels
- Trichoderma: green mold - no match
- Aspergillus: olive/green powdery - no match
- Gibberella: pink/red discoloration - no match
- Common Smut: black galls - no match
- Fusarium: partial white mycelium but scattered on orange kernels - partial match
- Diplodia_Ear_Rot (Corn_Disease_4 & 53): white mycelium filling between/around pale kernels - best visual match. The cross-sectional views show white cottony growth consistent with the test image's surface view

Diplodia Ear Rot produces dense white mycelium that fills the spaces between kernels and causes kernel discoloration/pale appearance. This matches the test image most closely.
